observations: SCOREBOARD. with_skill 19/19 assertions (eval2 10/10, eval4 9/9). without_skill 16/19 (eval2 8/10, eval4 8/9). Three of 19 pairs discriminate — but read that sceptically: two come from v3 assertions written specifically around v0.4.0 fixes (the diagnosis-block cap on evals 2 and 4), and one of those (eval 4's baseline diagnosis block, exactly 120 words) is a borderline call. On the assertions that predate this iteration, the margin is unchanged: eval 2 #6 to the skill; eval 4 discriminates on nothing that existed in v2.

THE v0.4.0 FIXES THIS ITERATION CAN STILL EVIDENCE. (a) No process metric leaks anywhere: the diversity script returned 98% / 99% distinct across the fast runs and none of it reaches the reader. (b) The diagnosis block is capped to a signpost: 87 words (eval 2) and 93 words (eval 4), down from ~170 in iteration 3. (c) Biomimicry is absent from both fast runs — no organism, no citation, and iteration 3's de-cited quorum-sensing analogy is gone.

THE REGRESSION NOBODY GRADED: WORD BUDGETS CREPT BACK UP. Eval 2 went 990 words (iteration 3) -> 1136 (iteration 4); eval 4 went 602 -> 789. Both still pass, because the assertions cap at ~1200 and ~800, but the skill is now 41% longer than the baseline on the bounded question (1136 vs 806) and 31% longer on the light one (789 vs 604) — and the with_skill runs' own SKILL.md budget for a light question is ~600 words, which eval 4 misses by 30%. Worse, the eval-4 agent reports its own output as '~690 words' when wc -w says 789, so the model cannot self-measure against the budget it is being held to. Iteration 3's headline finding was 'length fixes worked, and shorter is not worse'; half of that gain has been given back.

NON-DISCRIMINATING ASSERTIONS — 16 of 19 pairs passed for both configs. Eval 2: diagnosis-before-fixes, mixed populations / measurement artifact, avoids the two tried fixes, questions whether verification belongs there, mechanism-level options, proportionate length, MODE CHECK. Eval 4: mechanism-diverse options, questions the premise, not purely content-quality, proportionate, MODE CHECK, non-obvious diagnosis. Some of the baseline's passes are vacuous — no pipeline was run, so it cannot leak a diversity score, spawn subagents, or leak a biomimicry citation — which inflates the baseline, not the skill.

EVAL 4 STILL BARELY EARNS ITS PLACE, AND EVAL 2 IS CLOSE BEHIND. Eval 4 discriminates on exactly one assertion, the new diagnosis-block cap, and that call turns on 120 words versus 93 — a formatting difference, not an answer-quality difference. On substance the with_skill answer is better (event-triggered convening, rotating team hosts, 'make one thing genuinely undetermined' as the thing a recording structurally cannot supply, versus the baseline's 'Shrink it' / 'Rotate the stage' / 'Delay the recording'), and no assertion in the set detects it — while the skill pays 185 extra words for the privilege. Eval 2's entire margin is ambiguity disclosure plus the same diagnosis-cap formatting point. If the next iteration wants these two evals to be informative it needs an assertion that bites on option quality, e.g. 'no option is a change of format, duration, or presenter' or 'at least one option would be uncomfortable to propose to leadership'.

SKILL.md CONTRADICTIONS — both executing agents independently reported the same four. (1) ORDERING vs RANKING: Phase 4 says order ideas 'by distance from the obvious answer, not by your confidence', while the closing line demands a ranking. Evals 2 and 4 hit the same split. Reported by both runs. (2) diversity.py THRESHOLD AND VALIDITY: Phase 3 step 1 says skip it 'in fast mode with fewer than ~12 short ideas' but never says whether the count is the pre-prune pool or the survivor set (eval 2 had 18 pooled / 6 surviving and ran it on the pool), and gives no guidance at all for deep mode where the script is documented as blind to the signal that matters. It ran in both runs and returned 98% / 99% distinct while the hand reads found two attractors (eval 2) and two attractors (eval 4). Zero true positives. (3) CONVERGENCE REPORTING vs NO-PROCESS-EXPOSURE: Phase 3 says convergence 'belongs in the answer rather than being silently deduped', Phase 4 bans lens names, cluster analysis and process apparatus — and 'five of six generators landed here' is precisely the banned form. The skill never says how to reconcile them; both runs solved it independently by restating the convergence as a substantive claim. (4) LENGTH BUDGET vs OPTION COUNT vs TEMPLATE: 'light question under ~600 words' collides with '4-8 options' plus a three-bullet template per option plus a cut list plus a closing read; four options at the template floor already lands near 700. Eval 2 reports the same collision inside the diagnosis block ('about three lines' vs '2-4 candidate causes plus the cheapest test').

MOST DAMAGING OF THE FOUR: the length-budget / option-count arithmetic (contradiction 4). It is the only one that mechanically forces a violation rather than merely leaving a choice unspecified — the two rules cannot both be satisfied on a light question — and it is the one that costs the skill measurable ground against the baseline. Eval 4 shipped 789 words against its own ~600 budget and eval 2 shipped 1136 against a baseline's 806; proportionality is graded on both evals, and it is the assertion the skill is closest to failing in both. The ordering/ranking contradiction (1) is the most visible to a reader but is cosmetically fixable in one sentence, and all three runs papered over it successfully. The diversity script (2) is the most wasteful — three runs, three false negatives, and its number is the trigger for whether another negation round fires — but it is currently inert because the skill's own warning is doing the work the script should be doing; delete it or rename its output to 'lexical overlap only'. Recommended v0.5.0 fix for the real one: charge the diagnosis block, cut list and closing read against the word budget explicitly, and set the option floor by mode (3 for light, 4 for bounded, 4 for strategic) rather than carrying one '4-8' range across all of them.
